events.title: Warsh Holds Rates Steady at July FOMC, Cites AI Capex Surge
events.summary: Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates steady despite three dissenters voting for a hike. In the press conference, he emphasized that AI-related high-tech equipment and software capex is growing at nearly 20% year-over-year, calling it 'the most striking feature of the economy.' He framed the policy stance as a 'race between supply and demand' where AI investment is the dominant force.
events.dalioConnection: Step 14 (Printing Money): Warsh is choosing to hold rates rather than tighten into the AI capex cycle, effectively underwriting the buildout with accommodative monetary policy. This is directed monetary debasement — not panic, but strategic.
events.thesisConnection: Warsh is explicitly underwriting the AI arms race by holding rates steady underneath the capex cycle. His statement 'we haven't done much in 42 days. The markets have done quite a bit' signals he is letting the market adjust while he provides the monetary floor. This aligns with the counterattack strategy of steering forced foreign savings into productive AI capacity rather than consumption debt.
events.watch: Watch for dissent votes increasing (3 already). If AI capex fails to cool inflation while continuing to compound, Warsh may be forced to hike into the buildout — breaking the underwriter role. Watch the 4-quarter growth rate in AI equipment/software capex.

events.title: US Treasury Coordinates Yen Intervention Alongside BOJ
events.summary: The US Treasury stepped in alongside the Bank of Japan to defend the yen after it collapsed to its weakest level since 1986. Japan reportedly spent over $50 billion in a single day — likely the largest intervention on record. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent went on television to state the yen 'seems very undervalued' and that 'excess volatility in the yen isn't healthy.' A visible note at Camp David revealed a proposal for the US to buy $5-10 billion worth of yen.
events.dalioConnection: Step 13 (Large Debts): The US is not just managing its own debt burden — it is actively defending the funding pipe (yen carry trade) that provides marginal liquidity for US asset markets. The deficit/debt exists partly because foreign savings must be absorbed; Bessent is ensuring the absorption mechanism stays intact.
events.thesisConnection: The yen carry trade is the marginal dollar of liquidity for the entire AI buildout. Bessent knows that if markets connect the funding currency to the AI trade and start unwinding the pipe, the buildout loses its funding. His FX intervention is not about Japan — it is about preserving the liquidity pipe that flows into US AI assets. The visible note is intentional forward guidance.
events.watch: Watch BOJ bill vs. bond issuance (bills = liquidity export). Watch yen volatility and the Carry Trade Index correlation with equities. If Japan's new PM forces hawkishness to combat inflation, the pipe breaks.

events.title: China State Banks Absorbing Dollars at $700B/Year Pace, Official Reserves Flat
events.summary: Analysis by Brad Setser shows that while China's official FX reserves have been flat for over a decade, state banks have been absorbing dollars at a pace of roughly $700 billion per year through channels that do not count as official reserves. China's manufacturing surplus is now approximately 2% of world GDP — larger than Germany's and Japan's peaks combined.
events.dalioConnection: Step 8 (Strong Markets & Financial Centers): China's financial center is not open and deep like the US — it is a closed system weaponizing capital outflows. The 'strong markets' are actually a hidden pipeline forcing surplus savings into US assets.
events.thesisConnection: This is the core mechanism. The surplus is the largest it has ever been, recycled through hidden channels. The author calls this 'non-kinetic war' — pricing power over goods, rare earth chokepoints, and a slow bleed of purchasing power. The fact that almost nobody is talking about it tells you how well the design is working.
events.watch: Track Brad Setser's state bank FX accumulation data. Watch for any acceleration in hidden dollar absorption. Watch rare earth export controls as a visible escalation of the non-kinetic war.

events.title: Anthropic Files Confidentially for IPO at ~$50B Revenue Run Rate
events.summary: Anthropic has filed confidentially to go public after growing from a $9 billion revenue run rate to nearly $50 billion in approximately five months. The company is still burning cash heavily as compute bills compound faster than revenue. OpenAI is running near $25 billion in revenue while losing more than a dollar for every dollar earned.
events.dalioConnection: Step 2 (Inventiveness): Frontier labs represent America's attempt to leapfrog back to inventiveness — the core driver of rising empires. The AI race is the technological bet meant to reverse decline.
events.thesisConnection: Frontier labs are approaching the moment when private money stops being enough. They need public markets exactly as the window is slamming shut (SpaceX -20% from offer, semis worst month since GFC). The funding for the entire buildout is cross-collateralized — no leg can fail without pulling on every other. A Fed Chair underwriting capex and a Treasury Secretary defending the funding currency in the same week is not a coincidence.
events.watch: Watch IPO aftermarket performance. SpaceX is the proxy. If Anthropic/OpenAI cannot access public capital, the 'national security asset' becomes a funding crisis. Watch semiconductor index for leading signals.

The worst month since the GFC, combined with SpaceX's -20% IPO performance, signals the public capital window may be closing. events.title: Trump Tariffs in 2025 Crashed Markets but Served Structural Goal
events.summary: The Trump administration implemented broad tariffs in 2025 that crashed the stock market. The move was widely criticized as economically destructive, but in the context of the capital flow thesis, it served a structural purpose: adjusting around the core mechanical issue of China's surplus and dollar reserve status, even at the expense of short-term market performance.
events.dalioConnection: Step 15 (Internal Conflict): The tariffs caused internal conflict — markets crashed, commentators on left and right demonized the move, and the public debated symptoms. But the structural goal was addressing the core mechanism, not the symptom.
events.thesisConnection: The author explicitly cites this: 'The tariffs in 2025 that crashed the stock market didn't make sense to people because Trump implemented them at the expense of the stock market. Whether it causes a melt-up in financial assets or a melt-down, the priority is adjusting around the core mechanical issue.' This is policy structured around the mechanism, not the symptoms.
events.watch: Watch for future tariff or trade policy that hurts markets but serves structural goals. The pattern is: short-term pain for long-term capital flow realignment.

events.title: Chinese Household Consumption Remains Below 40% of GDP
events.summary: IMF data confirms Chinese household consumption remains below 40% of GDP, the lowest of any major economy. Roughly 40% of value created by Chinese workers returns to them as income, compared to closer to 70% in most major economies. Capped deposit rates have quietly transferred approximately 5% of GDP annually from household savers to state-connected borrowers.
events.dalioConnection: Step 7 (Strong Income Growth): In a normal rising empire, strong income growth lifts domestic demand. In China, income growth is deliberately suppressed to generate the surplus. This is not organic rise — it is engineered extraction.
events.thesisConnection: This is the root cause of the surplus. 'Income that never reaches households cannot be spent by households, so the excess production has to be sold to someone else.' The entire conflict is initiated by the CCP, and Chinese households are losing as badly as American workers. The suppression is visible in a single line: household consumption below 40% of GDP.
events.watch: Watch for any CCP policy shift toward household consumption (deposit rate liberalization, benefit reform for migrant workers, currency appreciation). Any such shift would reduce the surplus and change the capital flow dynamics.

events.title: BOJ Maintains Negative Real Rates, Continues Bill Issuance Over Bonds
events.summary: The Bank of Japan maintained its policy stance with short-end real rates remaining negative. The government continues to fund its growing deficit primarily through bill issuance rather than long-term bonds. This policy mix effectively exports liquidity to global markets, with an estimated $250 billion in direct cross-border yen borrowing and nearly $1 trillion when derivatives are included.
events.dalioConnection: Step 13 (Large Debts): Japan's debt-funded liquidity export is part of the global debt architecture. By issuing bills over bonds, Japan keeps the carry trade alive — providing the marginal funding for US asset markets.
events.thesisConnection: The BOJ is the marginal dollar of liquidity for the AI trade. 'As long as short-end real rates in Japan remain negative and they issue bills over bonds to fund their growing deficit, they are exporting liquidity to the world.' Japan cannot afford to be neutral in the US-China conflict because its monetary policy is the funding pipe for the AI buildout.
events.watch: Watch for any BOJ shift toward positive real rates or bond-heavy issuance. This would strangle the carry trade. Watch Japan's new PM — if inflation forces hawkishness, the liquidity pipe to US AI assets constricts.

events.title: Equal-Weighted S&P and NASDAQ at Historic Valuation Levels
events.summary: The NASDAQ and equal-weighted S&P 500 are trading at historic valuation levels. The standard explanation is 'euphoria,' but the author argues the mechanism is different: trillions of price-insensitive dollars are forced into US markets year after year, bidding up the price of all existing assets relative to their cash flows.
events.dalioConnection: Step 10 (Overextended): Historic valuations across the board (not just tech) signal an overextended financial system. The empire is absorbing more capital than it can productively deploy.
events.thesisConnection: 'Valuations are not high because investors lost their minds. They are high because the world's surplus has nowhere else to go.' This is a mechanical function of flows. The AI trade sits on top of this machine; it did not create it. Wall Street's core function is manufacturing things for that money to buy — and 2008 showed what happens when it runs out of legitimate product.
events.watch: Watch equal-weight S&P valuations (not just cap-weighted). If valuations compress while foreign inflows continue, it signals a shift in flow destination. Watch for a repeat of 2008-style 'manufactured assets' if legitimate product runs out.
